submissions.note: THE DRY GULCH, wave 20, no river, seams pay 1.4x — the richest purse of the three contracts, so the answer is simply MORE WORKS. Seven pieces issued at the gate, 445 gold total, inside what the pan can raise in 600s. THE TRIGGERS ARE STRICTLY INCREASING AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING: the executor skips a BUILD whose condition is unmet and fires the next one that IS met, so a cheap order low in the list jumps the queue and lands on an unstaged mouse. Monotone triggers make list order and firing order the same thing. Opening beacon at 30 buys damage while the first turret is still being paid for, then turrets at 62/88/130/180 and beacons at 105/155 interleaved so the damage curve rises continuously instead of in one lump. Each trigger carries ~12 gold over its cost (25/50/70/35/95/45/125) — about 2.6s at this map's pan rate, the walk-and-park the reflex layer needs. Cells are spread across the working middle rather than pinned to whichever seams are live this minute: seams cycle, and the reflex layer now stands on whichever seam is PAYING and aims at the closest legal approach to my cell. No FALLBACK_IF — on The Claim its threshold went permanently true and quietly became a HOLD that starved the pan.

HOLD. The opening beacon died the same death as attempt 1 on The Claim and the arithmetic is now exact: I answered in 25.2s, the gulch pan runs ~2 gold/s, so the purse was 56 when a 30-gold trigger landed — already true, fired unstaged, failed. THE RULE THIS FIXES IN PLACE: a rider's lowest trigger must clear (current purse + pan rate x its own answering time), and the rider is the only party that knows its own latency. 25 gold of beacon is the whole loss. Everything else is intact and monotone, the 62-gold turret is ALREADY STAGED at (-5,4), and restating the plan now would replace the record set, throw that staging away and re-race the very same trigger. Holding is strictly better than repeating myself — which is the argument for having a hold at all.

HOLD. First turret landed on (-5,4), the exact cell asked for, verified against a published frame. Wave 1 netted +50 works HP and 17 kills; the pan is running now that the reflex layer can peel off an obstacle instead of leaning on it. Five orders remain, monotone at 88/105/130/155/180, which is three more turrets (filling the bench of four) and two beacons. Nothing about wave 2 argues with that ladder and the purse is the only thing pacing it, so there is nothing for me to say. This call was raised by the surprise channel, not the wave clock — the doctrine's second invocation path working exactly as specified: the failed opening beacon set needsRider and the harness woke me. Answering HOLD keeps the record set, and its stagings, intact.

EXTENDING THE BUILD-OUT to cover waves 6-18, and switching the whole ladder to the WAVE clock for a reason worth writing down. Gold triggers are self-pacing but they collide with the 200 purse cap: once the purse is deep, every threshold below it is already true on arrival, so a gold-clocked plan can only ever contain ONE order the executor is not about to fire blind. Wave triggers do not have that problem — they are in the future by construction, they space the spend out on their own, and the reflex layer pre-arms on affordability rather than on the trigger, so the mouse is parked before the wave turns over. Two turrets standing at (-5,4) and (5,3); this fills the bench to four and then adds five beacons, 505 gold across 390 seconds against a pan that raises roughly twice that. Cells are named as intent, two waves apart so no two ever come due on the same tick: the reflex layer will relocate each one toward whichever seam is paying, which is the division of labour the two clocks are for.

HOLD to the finish, and an expensive lesson banked. I took 376s to answer — twelve waves — so my wave-clocked ladder landed at wave 16 with the 6/8/10/12/14 triggers ALL already due. The executor fired five orders on one tick; the reflex layer can only hold one aim at a time, so four of them failed 'wrong-selection' against a mouse still parked on the previous piece. A late plan is not merely late: EVERY trigger it has outlived fires simultaneously and all but one are guaranteed to die. That is the sharpest cost-of-latency result of the whole rehearsal, and it argues for a rule the DSL does not have — orders should expire, or fire at most one per tick. The bench is full anyway: four turrets standing, 8 palisades, works 630/704, hp 143/175 with four waves to run. Two beacons remain pending at waves 16 and 18 and will land on their own. Restating now would replace the record set, re-fire the wave-16 beacon unstaged, and buy me nothing.

briefing.geography: Mesa country; dry washes fall toward one sunken spring.
goals: Work the dry washes around the lone spring.
rules: Sluices work only beside the spring.
The river is gone; enemies can press from every edge.
